summary: Second peer roleplay session between the two closers, 25 minutes, late at night for Richard. Michael sets the agenda: he wants to drill isolating the real objection rather than the rebuttals. They run the $6,000 price reveal several times with Richard playing a prospect who has the money but did not expect the number, then run 'I need to think about it'. Richard teaches his framework — clarify whether it is capacity or uncertainty, score the goal 1-10 rather than the programme, then run the ABC of fear: admit, befriend, convert. Michael stops the session to take a sales call.
notable: Richard teaches a named framework, the 'ABC of fear — admit, befriend, convert', built on getting the prospect to concede that uncertainty is normal via an analogy, then converting with a past decision from their own life.

Richard coaches scoring the value of the goal rather than the programme — 'how important is your goal actually to you?' — and says he would talk a prospect out of buying at a 5: 'if it's only a five to you, like I wouldn't even advise you to do it because it's too much work anyway for a five'.
Richard explicitly warns against planting doubts a prospect has not raised — 'you don't want to speak that into someone's head, right?'

Richard debriefs a call from earlier the same day, a high performer who could afford the fee and did not buy: 'He was expecting three grand. It was six grand... he had it, and he feels like it's worth six grand, but he's just not doing it.'
Michael, a closer taking calls for the offer, discloses he has no savings and is running paycheck to paycheck — 'I gotta close some [deals], like, tomorrow kind of thing'.

Michael names payment plans as a live tool he needs to drill — 'how to actually say the proper thing to get them to be like, let's do a payment plan right now' — which sits against the Anthony Boon call two days earlier where no plan was structured.
Richard is 20 years old and is the senior coach in this pairing: 'And now you're being coached by a 20-year-old.' Michael: 'You could be 17. You could be 15, and I'll take your coaching.'
Sign-off references a 'Payments channel' used by the team.
